attaindesk.name: attainDesk
attaindesk.summary: attainDesk turns AI into one-click business operations for SMBs. Create social media content, product videos, marketing assets, research and grow business without specialist teams or AI expertise.

inspiration_intel.the_wedge: They assumed the expensive step (generation, review, data entry) should be priced before it runs.
inspiration_intel.what_it_does: attainDesk turns AI into one-click business operations for SMBs. Create social media content, product videos, marketing assets, research and grow business without specialist teams or AI expertise.
steal_this: Name the roles, give each a single responsibility and an output contract, and let the handoffs be where quality is enforced.
Take the constraint you were going to write a workaround for, and make it the headline. Broken-and-proud beats blocked-and-polished.
Ban the text box. When you need information, render 2-4 options. The product stops demanding literacy in your tool's language.
Pick the narrowest slice you can own, then fine-tune or rule-code it until it is unarguably better on that slice's eval.
inspiration_intel.naive_version_vs_this: A demo that needs the user to already know what to type. — then attainDesk made the step measurable, gated, or priced instead.
inspiration_intel.reuse_surface: portable to any agent that touches production data

audit.worth_note: Correct, useful, and unusually real: one of a handful of records in this catalog with paying customers attached to it, and the self-acquisition anecdote - their own Daily Digest surfaced local business groups, they used it for outreach, it produced the first paying customer - is the best argument in the whole page because it is a test they ran on themselves rather than a feature claim. Held to 'niche' for two reasons. The category is crowded here and elsewhere: Reeloli, Small Business AI Growth Desk and VibeMarketer are in this corpus with the same 'SMBs, no prompting, we do the marketing' pitch, so the wedge is execution, not insight. And nothing about the nine workflows is measured - no acceptance rate, no per-generation cost, no quality claim, no repository - so the record can support 'this team shipped a business' but not 'this mechanism works'. Breadth is also unpriced: nine generation pipelines is a maintenance commitment the page never accounts for.

artifact_exists.why: no source repo linked, but the page publishes a working artifact: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VGJBuZq8FtY

build_is_real.why: no repository published, so the build cannot be read

limits_disclosed.why: the challenges section discloses operating constraints (what the pipeline costs to run and to iterate on), but no accuracy, coverage or failure-mode limit; the future-work section implies the remaining open edges

numbers_add_up.why: 2 figure(s) a reader can check against the product (first subscription revenue on a $49/month (+taxes) plan; nine guided workflows plus a Daily Digest from one workspace), but 3 headline figure(s) carry no testable denominator: 13 real businesses using attainDesk; $0 in paid marketing spend to reach those businesses

stack_consistency.why: no repo to cross-check the declared stack against

test_or_eval_evidence.why: the only testing sentence on the page is a denial (no suite, set or run is linked)

assumptions: an acceptance standard per workflow, written down before shipping, because nothing in the capture defines what a good generated asset is and without one 'quality' is unfalsifiable
a cost model per generation (tokens, seconds of video, retries) priced against $49/month before adding any video-heavy workflow, since the page never publishes one
distribution assumed to be the hard part: the record's own growth was founder-led and organic, so a clone inherits the product and not the 13 customers
brand-context persistence (logos, headshots, style) needs a store and a review path if outputs are to be reusable rather than regenerated
clone_cost.estimate: 3-4 weeks per workflow a business would actually pay for, and the ninth is not nine times cheaper than the first
clone_cost.why: The generation plumbing is commodity: Gemini text and image endpoints, Veo for video, TTS for voiceover, Search grounding for the digest, all of it behind Cloud Functions and Cloud Tasks with Firestore for job state - a small team can stand up two or three of these in a month, and the page says its own build was substantially done with Gemini coding agents and Antigravity, which is a claim about speed of authoring, not about defensibility. What is not commodity is the per-vertical taste that makes each output acceptable - what a staged living room has to look like for a listing agent to send it, how a menu photo has to be lit - plus auth, billing, analytics and the trust required for a business to hand a workspace its brand. And the acquisition story the record actually claims as its accomplishment is founder-led outreach at $0 spend, which cannot be cloned at all: the moat named in the page is the team's ability to sell to SMBs, not the pipeline.

audit.what_to_steal: Refuse the prompt box. The stated design principle - users describe a business outcome while model selection, prompting, context and iteration happen behind the scenes - is transferable to any vertical agent, and the async plumbing that makes it survivable is the second half: Cloud Functions plus Cloud Tasks so a two-second text job and a two-minute video job share one UI contract with Firestore holding job state. Then steal the honesty of the product framing itself: 'the best AI experience can sometimes feel like there is less AI, not more' is the line to put on a wall in any team shipping a model-backed workflow, and the Digest-that-found-the-first-customer loop is a template for pointing your own research surface at your own acquisition problem.
audit.what_breaks_first: Unit economics on the expensive workflows, then the quality question nobody measured. A $49/month plan is priced against a catalogue that includes Veo-class video generation and image editing for every customer; one realtor rendering a dozen listings a week can out-earn the subscription in inference on its own, and the page publishes no per-generation cost, latency or failure rate - while simultaneously admitting that some operations are computationally intensive and asynchronous, i.e. it knows exactly where the exposure is. Second: nine workflows means nine vendor surfaces, each with its own silent quality drift, and there is no acceptance metric for any of them, so a model version bump changes what a customer receives with nothing in the loop to notice. Third: '13 businesses using it' has no denominator - not paying, not retained, not per-workflow - so the traction claim that carries the record cannot be turned into a rate by a reader at all.

prior_art.relation: same buyer, same event, same subsystem, opposite shape: Reeloli goes deep on one channel (WhatsApp, 15 days of local-business marketing video, planned and produced by AI) where attainDesk goes broad across nine workflows in a web workspace - read the pair together for the depth-versus-breadth trade a horizontal SMB product has to answer

the same pitch stated as a category rather than a product - 'marketing, content, outreach and operational assets in minutes' - which is the generic prompt-box attainDesk's page explicitly argues against
attainDesk's missing half: VibeMarketer closes the loop with persistent brand context, approval before campaigns go out, and provider-confirmed publishing, where attainDesk generates and stops

one workflow, priced honestly: photo to print-ready sketch for print-on-demand sellers, live in production - the same 'guided outcome, no prompting' bet at a tenth of the surface area, which is the argument for starting narrow

greenlight-nine-agent-production-crew.name: Greenlight - Nine-Agent Production Crew
greenlight-nine-agent-production-crew.summary: Nine agents turn a screenplay into a film - reading, casting, prompting, shooting, checking their own footage - and quote you the cost and the odds before spending a cent.

inspiration_intel.the_wedge: They built the thing that survives the no-budget, no-internet, no-permission case.
inspiration_intel.what_it_does: Nine agents turn a screenplay into a film - reading, casting, prompting, shooting, checking their own footage - and quote you the cost and the odds before spending a cent.
steal_this: Model your most expensive operation as a priced quote with an expected-retry figure. Users forgive slowness, not surprise bills.
Name the roles, give each a single responsibility and an output contract, and let the handoffs be where quality is enforced.
Log the verdict (keep/again, accept/reject) next to the input, and tell users their own history now drives the estimate.
Classify each step as judgement vs. format vs. volume, then route. Save the frontier model for the one call everything downstream depends on.
inspiration_intel.naive_version_vs_this: A demo that needs the user to already know what to type. — then Greenlight - Nine-Agent Production Crew made the step measurable, gated, or priced instead.
inspiration_intel.reuse_surface: portable to any agent that touches production data

audit.worth_note: The wedge is not 'AI video' — it is pricing a generation step before you commit and then making your own logged outcomes the estimator. That transfers to anything with an expensive call (image gen, agent runs, transcription at volume). Not 'breakthrough' only because it ships as one team's v1 with no public code to adopt.

artifact_exists.why: no source repo linked, but the page publishes a working artifact: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sS_gIU9flCE

build_is_real.why: no repository published, so the build cannot be read

limits_disclosed.why: the team stated where the system fails, in production terms (drift, fail)

numbers_add_up.why: first-pass success 29% before casting → 49% after (recomputed: 20 points of success for $0.02 of candidates; expected retry cost falls $1.86 → $1.17); cost ladder: $0.02 candidate / $1 shot / $20 segment (recomputed: a 12-shot chapter quoted at ~$4.50 is consistent with ~$0.375/shot at the tier used, i.e. the ladder is not the naive 12×$1)

stack_consistency.why: no repo to cross-check the declared stack against

test_or_eval_evidence.why: a measured evaluation with a stated denominator is described on the page (an A/B comparison or a logged-outcome harness counts; a bare 'we tested it' does not)

assumptions: assume 1 engineer + 1 designer, 6 weeks, and real spend money for the generation ladder (their full film priced ~$238)
you can start smaller: one shot class, one priced gate, one table of verdicts — the calibration view is what takes the weeks
the character-reference locking is the part that needs image-model skill, not plumbing
clone_cost.why: the agent choreography is a weekend; the honest parts are the ledger, the calibration views, and the locked-identity image pipeline

audit.what_to_steal: Two moves, and they compose: (1) quote the cost and the pass rate before the button, and push every hesitation down the price ladder (settle a character at $0.02, not $1); (2) log every verdict row into a store you can query, then let the estimate switch from your priors to the user's own measured numbers and label which one they are reading, with sample size. Also steal 'the money gate is a schema transition, not a prompt'.
audit.what_breaks_first: The success-rate estimate. Below a few hundred logged shots per shot class the displayed percentage is a prior wearing a lab coat, so build the calibration view (predicted vs observed) in week one or you are shipping confidence theatre. Second to break: prompt-injection-free subtitle burn-in on a fresh container, which is exactly the bug they documented (ffmpeg exits 0 with no fonts).

prior_art.relation: also a multi-agent production crew, but it does not price the shot or learn from kept/rejected takes
same orchestration shape, no cost model
independent verification of a generated artifact; Greenlight does the weaker version (counts people in frame) and then feeds it into the retry
